text:
Good morning, and a very pleasant Saturday to you. 

First, the news from home.

Story one. The opposition New Patriotic Party is holding its National Delegates Conference today at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, where over seven thousand one hundred delegates are gathering to elect new national executives. As reported across MyJoyOnline, Starr F M, and Three News, between three thousand and four thousand police officers have been deployed to secure the city and manage traffic. Party figures have brushed aside recent polling forecasts, with candidates such as Paul Afoko stressing that reconciliation and party unity will be the real deciding factors for delegates ahead of the twenty twenty-eight elections.

Story two. The Economic and Organised Crime Office has announced that it is working with the Attorney-General to bring the former Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, before a weekend court for bail. Three News and Starr F M report that the detention has triggered strong political backlash, with Alexander Afenyo-Markin accusing the N D C government of acting like an overzealous police officer determined to make an arrest at all costs. Legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has also questioned the necessity of keeping Baffour Awuah in custody when he had not attempted to abscond.

Story three. The Social Security and National Insurance Trust has defended its demolition of unauthorised structures along the Labadi beach front, stating that National Security was called in to protect vital state hospitality assets belonging to Ghanaian workers and pensioners. According to Three News, the demolition has provoked sharp political criticism, with Vice President Mahamudu Bawumia describing the action as wanton destruction and pledging that the N P P will rebuild the area and grant formal leases to affected local businesses.

Now, around the world.

Story four. Tensions in the Horn of Africa have escalated sharply after Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic ties, as reported by B B C News Africa and France Twenty-Four. The complete breakdown in relations comes as the Ethiopian military battles rebel forces across its northern region, prompting the African Union to urgently appeal for restraint from all parties.

Story five. In South Africa, a new report cited by Africa News reveals that suspected political assassinations have claimed at least forty-three lives this year ahead of upcoming local government elections. The surge in targeted killings comes with the local polls just one month away, raising serious security alarms across the country's political landscape.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
